name: Saint Pius V
history: A Dominican friar from a poor family who became pope in 1566 and put the reforms of the Council of Trent into effect. He issued the Roman Catechism, the reformed Breviary and the Missal of 1570, and lived as austerely as a friar. He called Christendom to pray the Rosary before the victory of Lepanto in 1571.
life: Antonio Ghislieri was born at Bosco, near Alessandria, and kept sheep as a boy. He entered the Dominicans at fourteen, taking the name Michele, and taught theology for years. He served as an inquisitor, then as bishop and cardinal, and was elected pope in 1566. He set about carrying out the decrees of Trent: he published the Roman Catechism, reformed the Breviary and the Missal, insisted that bishops live in their dioceses, cleared the papal court of luxury and named Saint Thomas Aquinas a Doctor of the Church. He went on wearing his white Dominican habit, from which, tradition says, comes the white cassock of the popes. He visited hospitals and washed the feet of the poor. Facing the advance of the Ottoman fleet, he formed the Holy League and asked all Christendom to pray the Rosary. He died on 1 May 1572 and was canonised in 1712.
prayerTo: Saint Pius, shepherd and reformer, you lived simply in the midst of great power and gave the Church the treasures of her worship. Pray for the Pope and the bishops, for the reform of the Church in every age, and for me, that I may begin with the reform of my own life. Amen.
penance: Pray a decade of the Rosary today for peace in the world. Pius lived on simple food: keep your meals plain today and give something to the poor.
meditation: He kept the habit of a friar on the throne of Peter. What habit of simplicity could you keep in the midst of your own comforts?
